traits.bark_colour.note: The bark colour chosen by eye for appearance (see its note), as a screen colour: it stood as appearance.bark [0.4, 0.33, 0.25], which is linear light, so the trunk drew pale grey to white beside photographs of the species (2026-10-23). It stands here in sRGB, as bark colours are picked, and the bark rule (tracheophyta) turns it into linear light.

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS (Corylus cornuta): California hazelnut (var. californica) flowers from January to March on the Willamette, Mount Hood and Siuslaw National Forests of western Oregon. Too few iNaturalist records in the Puget Sound lowlands are annotated as flowering to count (17).

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Corylus cornuta): nuts ripe from August to November in the west coast states and British Columbia, falling when fully ripe in the autumn.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Corylus californica: a loose spreading shrub 2 m to 3.5 m high.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923), as Corylus californica: leaves 3.5 cm to 8 cm long.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Corylus cornuta (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.53 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.53, branches 0.51. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long. Fitted so the tallest of five plants (seeds 1 to 5) stays within Abrams vol. 1 (1923, as Corylus californica): 2 to 3.5 m tall. Fitted to the oldest reference size at 2.09, plants reached 3.63 m at 15 years.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall, many-stemmed shrub with broad, doubly toothed, soft leaves in two rows and nuts in bristly beaked husks. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 3.5 m tall at 15 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: soft mid-green leaves; smooth grey-brown stems. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: nuts in pairs, each in a green, bristly husk drawn out into a long beak. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: yellow catkins in February and March; nuts in green husks through the summer, ripe in August and September. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth grey-brown bark with lenticels; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): an understory shrub: broad shade leaves, smaller and more sharply toothed in sun; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
